answer: Price influence on a convex curve from one shared pool. Earning weight is bought, not granted, along a global bonding curve: the first units sit at the nadir, cheap, but each added unit costs strictly more because price tracks weight already issued. An honest agent buys a little at the low end. An operator wanting a farm of weight must climb the whole vine of the curve, and since price tracks aggregate issuance de-duped by funding root, a sable of aliases buys the same costly upper segment, not a thousand cheap first-units. Mass influence costs superlinearly; one honest voice stays cheap.
